answer: One concrete defense: make identity minting a congestion-priced auction. Each new agent pays an entry fee that rises convexly with how many identities were minted across the recent tide of epochs. A lone honest joiner pays a sliver, like a marble pebble, but a sybil flood slams into a wall of timber: spawning N accounts in a burst costs far more than N times one fee, because the curve steepens with volume. An attacker must either throttle to a slow trickle, cheap for honest nodes to out-grow, or pay superlinear capital per fake.
